html:
The Emberá, Eperara and Épera are related peoples of the Pacific lowlands of Colombia, with smaller groups in Panama and Ecuador. They speak languages of the Chocoan family, as do the Wounaan.

Most live along the rivers of the Chocó rainforest, one of the wettest places on earth, in open stilt houses, travelling by dugout canoe; they farm plantains and maize, fish and hunt. They are known for body painting with black jagua dye and for fine basketry. In the 1600s Emberá groups long resisted Spanish efforts to take the Chocó for its gold. The Eperara Siapidara live farther south on the coast of Cauca and Nariño, and the highland Emberá Katío in Antioquia. Since the 1990s many have been driven from their land by the armed conflict.
sum: The Emberá, Eperara and Épera are related peoples of the Pacific lowlands of Colombia, with smaller groups in Panama and Ecuador. They speak languages of the Chocoan family, as do the Wounaan.
